source_evidence.anchor: E2: finite-p formula and p=infinity extension
source_evidence.observation: For 0<p<infinity, norm(X,Lp)=(E|X|^p)^(1/p); for p=infinity it is ess sup |X|.

source_evidence.location: PDF p.2; printed p.6; Section 1.1, opening paragraphs
source_evidence.anchor: E3: definition and vector-space status of Lp
source_evidence.observation: Lp(Omega,Sigma,P) consists of random variables with finite Lp norm; for p in [1,infinity] it is called a normed Banach space.

source_evidence.location: PDF p.2; printed p.6; Section 1.2, Eq. (1.4)
source_evidence.observation: For every p in [1,infinity] and X,Y in Lp, norm(X+Y,Lp)<=norm(X,Lp)+norm(Y,Lp); no further hypotheses are stated.

source_evidence.location: PDF p.2; printed p.6; Section 1.2, sentence after Eq. (1.4)
source_evidence.observation: The equation is identified as the triangle inequality for the Lp norm.

binders: p in [1,infinity], including p=1 and p=infinity. [E2,E4]
Real-valued random variables X,Y on Omega. [E1,E4]
hypotheses: X,Y in Lp(Omega,Sigma,P), so both norms are finite. [E3,E4]
definitions_and_conventions: Lp contains the random variables of finite Lp norm; X+Y is their pointwise sum. [E3,E4]
implicit_context: X and Y share one probability space and Lp exponent. [E3,E4]
Measurability is implicit in random variable. [E1]
No independence, sign, centering, or distributional relation is assumed. [E4]

details: Universal in p in [1,infinity] and X,Y in Lp; both endpoints are included. [E2,E4]
Lp membership restricts the claim to finite input norms. [E3,E4]
All norms use the same p and space; the result is the triangle inequality. [E4,E5]

undebatable_constraints: Require X,Y in the same Lp, hence finite input norms. [E3,E4]
Add no independence, sign, centering, or distribution hypotheses. [E4]

ambiguities.issue: The source does not say whether Lp elements are functions or almost-sure equivalence classes.
ambiguities.evidence: It calls Lp a vector space of random variables and the quantity a norm without stating a quotient convention. [E3]
ambiguities.impact: This affects object equality because almost-surely equal representatives have zero distance, but not Eq. (1.4)'s numerical inequality.

contract_plain_english: For p from 1 through infinity and finite-norm X,Y in the same Lp space, the norm of X+Y is at most the sum of their norms; p=infinity uses essential supremum, and no further probabilistic assumptions apply. [E2-E4]
